target.title: fix(codex): isolated cron reports Codex startup stalls
target.body:
Related #84567 and #64744.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where isolated cron runs routed through Codex could report a generic setup/startup timeout when Codex app-server startup had already reached the required `initialize` protocol request and then stalled. That made the user-visible failure look like `isolated agent setup timed out before runner start` instead of identifying the Codex initialize phase that owned the blocked startup.

The reporter path is #84567's isolated cron setup-timeout route for `openai/gpt-5.5` / Codex routing. #64744 provides the older Codex initialize-hang context. This PR does not auto-close #84567 because a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn is still not claimed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the existing startup budget but carries the remaining deadline into the Codex app-server client startup owner, where it is consumed only around `client.initialize()`. That lets `codex app-server initialize timed out` win once startup has reached `initialize`, while pre-initialize factory/start-context hangs still use the generic startup timeout path.

This conflict-resolution update rebases the PR onto current `origin/main` and adapts the original deadline wiring to main's current `shared-client.ts` factory-options contract. It intentionally preserves main's removal of `client-factory.ts` and does not reintroduce the older active-lease notification hook that no longer exists on the current client contract.

Out of scope: OAuth profile selection, provider/model routing, successful Codex app-server startup behavior, post-`thread/start` turn execution, user config, schema, protocol payloads, public APIs, and any claim that the reporter's live/idle worker snapshot alone proves the exact stall was inside `client.initialize()`.

## User Impact

Codex startup attempts that reach `initialize` and then stall now fail at the initialize lifecycle boundary with a more specific diagnostic, instead of being masked by the broader startup watchdog. Operators and maintainers get clearer failure attribution for isolated cron Codex startup stalls before `thread/start`.

The highest-risk area is Codex app-server startup availability, because timeout ordering and connection-closed retry ownership change around the first protocol request. The mitigation is narrow: callers that omit the internal initialize deadline keep the previous factory-wide timeout behavior, and retries stop only after the outer startup watchdog has already abandoned startup.

## Evidence

Earlier proof retained from the PR:

- Real-stdio stalled initialize proof: a spawned Codex app-server child received the real `initialize` request, did not answer, and OpenClaw raised `codex app-server initialize timed out` rather than the generic startup timeout. This proof uses a deterministic real-stdio stalled app-server child, not reporter-only OAuth credentials.
- Isolated cron proof: the real isolated cron `agentTurn` route for `openai/gpt-5.5` selects the Codex harness, preserves the `openai-codex:default` profile id, attributes an initialize stall to the Codex app-server initialize phase, and reaches `thread/start` after a successful initialize response.
- Live local OAuth setup proof from the earlier proof round showed managed Codex app-server setup completed `initialize` and returned idle `thread/start`; it did not start a model turn and is not a full reporter-account recurring cron/provider turn.

Validation run after rebasing onto current `origin/main` and resolving conflicts:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.9 [local path redacted]

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  10 passed (10)
  Duration  27.50s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 251.19s
```

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.9 [local path redacted]

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
  Duration  66.60s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 78.90s
```

```text
pnpm check:no-conflict-markers

$ node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs
```

Attempted but not counted as passing validation:

```text
pnpm check:changed

[check:changed] delegating to Blacksmith Testbox via `pnpm crabbox:run`.
[crabbox] selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
```

That failure occurred before repository checks ran, at the local crabbox/Blacksmith wrapper sanity check. The focused Codex app-server regression, isolated cron regression, and conflict-marker check passed after the rebase.
